finding.summary: Blank-cell skipping in `Arguments.iterate` applies to every range-consuming function, not just aggregations, silently changing/breaking positional and blank-counting semantics
finding.evidence: arguments.ts: `const isRange = isSrng(node.v); ... if (isRange) { const cell = grid.get(ref); if (!cell || cell.v === undefined || cell.v === '') continue; }`. The skip is unconditional for all range args of all functions that go through `Arguments.iterate`, so (a) functions with positional semantics over a range (MATCH/INDEX/VLOOKUP/HLOOKUP-style, or any function relying on the yielded cell count/order matching the range shape) now see a compacted sequence with shifted indices; (b) COUNTBLANK/COUNTA-style functions over a range can no longer observe blanks and will return 0/wrong counts; (c) previously-passing bounded-range behavior (`=AVERAGE(A1:A5)` with blanks counted as 0) changes for all existing formulas. Nothing in the diff restricts the skip to aggregation functions.
